title: J. C. Heard joins Cab; Cozy Cole to CBS; Art Tatum at the Big Log
summary: Hinton and Jones recall Cozy Cole's leaving Cab Calloway for CBS in 1943, and an evening in California with Art Tatum's trio.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Just hold it for a second while I change tape because we got a couple drummers I think we're going to talk about. So you were talking about J. C. Heard and when he joined Cab's band when Cozy had left to go to CBS. John Hammond finally got some things going where they would use some black people -

Dave Dexter, John Hammond, Raymond Scott - we were at Rockefeller Center. You was playing the Strand Theatre. I came to the Strand Theatre; I said, "Cozy, you are going to play with Raymond Scott at CBS." He said, "I'm with Fess." I said, "You're going to have to leave." Shortly after that - you know sometimes when we get into California there'd be 3 or 4 bands and you look up and you've got Cab, Duke, and Basie, and all of us will be there together. When we get there you know good and well that Cozy and I were hanging out. We were going up to Big Log where Art Tatum would Chicken sit up there with Slam Stewart and what's-his-name. This was in '43. It's got to be because that's when

Art got the trio with Tiny Grimes. Tiny Grimes had a little four-string guitar and he was scared to death. He hadn't been playing for about 9 months and he's sitting up there — But they was playing "The Streets of Paris". I said, "Cozy, you have to go."
